key_insight: Hybrid quantum-classical PINNs had 38–44% fewer parameters but took at least 10× longer than the classical PINN at every measured stage.
engineering_relevance: Benchmark wall-clock time and derivative costs rather than using parameter count as a proxy for computational efficiency.
method: Tested a classical PINN, four hybrid configurations, and size-matched classical controls on 1D seawater temperature diffusion.
Timed cumulative forward, first- and second-order input-gradient, and PDE-loss parameter-gradient stages with CPU-simulated quantum circuits.
Varied qubit count, circuit depth, and batch size; compared two simulator backends for circuit-only forward execution.
evidence_signal: Hybrids were 14–56× slower on forward passes and 10–97× slower on PDE-loss parameter gradients than the classical PINN, remaining 9–85× slower than size-matched controls.
watch_item: Results concern one benchmark and CPU simulation; performance on quantum hardware or other workloads is not established.
paper_title: Fewer Parameters, Longer Runtimes: The Wall-Clock Cost of Hybrid Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks
